title: Simple Pendulum
subject: physics
aim: To find the acceleration due to gravity g from the L–T² graph of a simple pendulum.
theory:
For small oscillations (amplitude under about 10°) a simple pendulum swings with period

$$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$$

so $T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{g}L$. A graph of $L$ against $T^2$ is a straight line through the origin with slope $\frac{g}{4\pi^2}$.
procedure: Set the effective length L (thread length plus bob radius).
Displace the bob slightly (under 10°) and release it.
Time 20 complete oscillations and divide by 20 to get T.
Record the reading and repeat for at least five lengths.
Plot L against T² and compute g from the slope.
precautions: Start timing as the bob passes the mean position.
Make sure the bob swings in one vertical plane.

viva.question: Why must the amplitude be small?
viva.answer: T = 2π√(L/g) assumes sin θ ≈ θ, which is only accurate for small angles.

viva.question: Does the period depend on the mass of the bob?
viva.answer: No. The period depends only on L and g.

viva.question: What is a seconds pendulum?
viva.answer: A pendulum with a period of 2 s; its length is about 99.4 cm on Earth.

viva.question: Why time 20 oscillations instead of one?
viva.answer: It spreads the reaction-time error over many swings, which reduces the error in T.
